clue.text: Get rid of souvenir of gambling with the Devil?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, used for the Devil or Hell
a playing card is a keepsake of a game of chance

explanation.surface: A gambler keeps a memento from a card game played against Satan himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DIS CARD, the card from a game against Dis; 'with' joins the pieces, which go in answer order with the Devil's name first.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard something is to throw it away as unwanted, which is to get rid of it.

clue.text: Sadness is beginning to moderate in time

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the word for time

parts.note: a day is a period of time

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of moderate

explanation.surface: Grief starts to ease with time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ISM inside DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is distress and disappointment, close to sadness.

clue.text: Agree to fix story expressing source of alibi

parts.note: to set is to fix

indicators.note: expressing means squeezing out, so the letter is pressed out of the story

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: source of picks the first letter of alibi

explanation.surface: A suspect agrees to concoct a story to back up an alibi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressing' squeezes A out of TALE, leaving TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a dispute is to agree terms, so settle means agree.

clue.text: High point in a narrow-minded proposition about love

parts.note: po is informal for prim or narrow-minded, as in po-faced

indicators.note: about means the proposition goes around the letter for love

parts.note: a thesis is a proposition put forward
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: The peak of an argument made by a narrow-minded person about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside THESIS, giving THEOSIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An apotheosis is the culmination or peak of something, its high point.

clue.text: Elevated Old Masters finally — including me?

definitions.text: Elevated Old Masters finally — including me?

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue means lifted up, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: old means aged

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Masters

explanation.surface: An artist asks whether he too counts among the revered Old Masters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' turns AGED into DEGA. The whole clue is the artist speaking: Edgar Degas wondering if the Old Masters include him.
explanation.definitionFit: Degas, the French Impressionist painter, could claim a place among the great painters of the past.

clue.text: Well-worn stuff given to horse?

parts.note: corn is hackneyed, over-familiar material, as in corny jokes
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: Tired old fodder handed out to a horse in its stable.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a corncob is the sort of stuff you might feed to a horse, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob is an ear of maize, plausible feed for a horse, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Excavator runs in pursuit of one claim in rocky situation

indicators.note: in pursuit of means the letter comes after the other pieces
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of one claim are shaken up

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A prospector chases a claim in difficult terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in rocky situation' rearranges ONE CLAIM to COALMINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal miner digs coal out of the ground, so is literally an excavator.

clue.text: Cycling without restriction rocks?

indicators.note: cycling means the first letter goes round to the end

parts.note: free means unrestricted

explanation.surface: Riding a bike with no limits over rough rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' moves the F of FREE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rocks near the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Church expert accepts regularly using note in musical form

indicators.note: accepts means the expert takes in the following letters

parts.note: an ace is an expert
on means taking a drug regularly, as in on painkillers

explanation.surface: A church music expert takes on a particular note in a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts ONN inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaconne is a slow dance-based musical form built on a repeated bass line.

clue.text: Happen to collar servant producing evidence of injury

indicators.note: to collar is to grab, so the word for happen holds the servant

parts.note: to be is to exist or take place, to happen
a lackey is a servant

explanation.surface: A servant gets grabbed by the neck and ends up hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to collar' places LACKEY between B and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A black eye is bruising round the eye, a visible sign of a blow.

clue.text: Affix scrap

definitions.meaning: to apply or fix it in place

explanation.surface: Two bare words: stick on, or fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a minor fight, and setting a thing to another fastens it on.

clue.text: A crippled vessel returned after circumnavigating a country

indicators.note: circumnavigating means sailing right round, so the reversed phrase goes around the second a
returned says the whole crippled-vessel phrase is read backwards

parts.note: crippled means lame
a tug is a small boat

explanation.surface: A disabled ship limps home after sailing round some unnamed place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns A LAME TUG into GUTEMALA, and 'circumnavigating' wraps that round the second A; 'after' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a nation of Central America.

clue.text: Compound of lethal arsenic returned by the writer nevertheless

indicators.note: a chemical compound combines elements, so the letters of lethal are mixed up
returned means the chemical symbol is turned back to front

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A writer of a poison mystery mixes a deadly arsenic compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound of' makes ALLTHE from LETHAL; 'returned' turns AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: All the same is an idiom meaning however or nonetheless, the same as nevertheless.

clue.text: What allows boats to advance forward?

definitions.meaning: a canal ... lets boats move on between water levels
a forward in rugby union, in the second row of the scrum

explanation.surface: What lets boats move onward?
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' seems to belong with 'advance', but it is a second definition: a rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock raises or lowers canal boats, and a lock is also a second-row player in the rugby pack.

clue.text: Deliveries seized by mischievous beggar

indicators.note: seized by means the cricket word is held inside the mischievous word

parts.note: impish means mischievous
an over is six deliveries in cricket

explanation.surface: A prankster beggar grabs the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beggar' is a verb, to make poor, not a noun. In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end, hence 'Deliveries'.
explanation.definitionFit: To beggar someone is to reduce them to poverty, which is to impoverish.

clue.text: Going out of business, only going through my cash

parts.note: a firm that folds closes down

indicators.note: one word going through another sits inside it

parts.note: only one, as in the only one; one means single or only

explanation.surface: A collapsing firm leaves someone with only their money passing through their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' appears twice with different jobs: the first is part of the business phrase, the second part of the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding money is banknotes, as opposed to coins, so it means cash.

clue.text: Velocities in opposite directions in astronomical region

indicators.note: in opposite directions means one velocity word runs backwards and the other forwards

parts.note: speed and pace are both rates of motion, so the one word supplies two velocity words
pace is a rate of movement, the second velocity the plural word supplies

explanation.surface: Objects moving at speed in opposite directions through some region of the cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Velocities' supplies two words, SPEED and PACE; 'in opposite directions' reads SPEED backwards as DEEPS while PACE runs forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep space is the vast expanse beyond the Earth's neighbourhood, a region studied by astronomers.

clue.text: Economic competition in Edwardian times perhaps absorbing one chapter

indicators.note: absorbing means the period word takes in the next letters

parts.note: the Edwardian era preceded the First World War, so was pre-war
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A history of trade rivalry in the Edwardian era takes one chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edwardian times perhaps' is a definition by example: the Edwardian years (1901-1910) came before the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A price war is cut-throat rivalry between firms undercutting each other's prices.

clue.text: Disorderly commune securing current praise

indicators.note: securing means the jumble holds the next letter firmly inside
disorderly means jumbled, so the letters of commune are rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An unruly commune wins praise for getting its electricity running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorderly' turns COMMUNE into ENCOMUM; 'securing' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An encomium is a formal speech or piece of writing full of high praise.

clue.text: Computer message repeatedly right about routine more prone to bugs, nothing less

indicators.note: about means the doubled letter goes around the rest
repeatedly says the abbreviation for right is used twice over
something prone to bugs malfunctions, so the letters are jumbled
less says a letter is removed from the jumbled pool

parts.note: O is the round figure nothing

explanation.surface: A programmer complains that a routine full of bugs keeps producing a right mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prone to bugs' scrambles ROUTINE MORE and 'less' removes an O, leaving UNTIMEERRO; 'about' places that between RR, R from 'right' twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-time error is an alert a program displays when it fails while executing.

clue.text: Criminal charge — appeal regularly dismissed? Go downhill fast

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap

indicators.note: regularly dismissed means every other letter of appeal is dropped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A criminal charge stands when the appeal is routinely thrown out, and the case collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first, third and fifth letters of APPEAL leaves PEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To rappel is to abseil, descending a rock face quickly on a rope.

clue.text: That man will get tense when cornered by my warrior

parts.note: he means that man

indicators.note: when cornered by means the tense letter is trapped inside the exclamation

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A man gets anxious when trapped by a soldier of mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, like 'cor', British slang for 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector was the Trojan champion of the Iliad, the greatest warrior of Troy.

clue.text: Chill, mostly icy, around zero

indicators.note: around means the trimmed word is wrapped about the next letter
mostly means all but the last letter of the word for icy

parts.note: icy means cold
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A wintry chill, almost freezing, hovering around zero degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts COLD to COL.
explanation.definitionFit: To cool something is to make it less warm, the same as to chill it.

clue.text: Claim donkey continually grazed

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
ever means always or continually
grazed means ate

explanation.surface: A donkey that keeps on grazing all day long.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to declare or affirm solemnly, which is to claim.

clue.text: Fifteen letters will fix hard code

indicators.note: will fix means the run of letters takes the next letter fixed inside it

parts.note: E to S is a run of fifteen letters of the alphabet, E through S inclusive
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A long word will fix a hard puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to read 'Fifteen letters' as an alphabet range: E through S inclusive spans fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the guiding beliefs or moral code of a person or group.

clue.text: Place for claret, French drink seen around Spain

indicators.note: seen around means the drink is placed around the next letter

parts.note: vin is French for wine
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A French wine served round Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is slang for blood, so its place is a vein, not a wine glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein carries blood, which is jokingly called claret.

clue.text: A little nonsense removing the old deception

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount

indicators.note: removing says the old word for the is taken out

parts.note: eyewash is nonsense or humbug
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Cutting out the stale material from a bit of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes YE from EYEWASH, leaving EWASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitewash is a cover-up that hides faults or wrongdoing, so a deception.

clue.text: This person, crazy to seize power, received information

parts.note: this person is the speaker, I

indicators.note: to seize means the crazy one grabs and holds the next letter

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A self-described madman plans to seize power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to seize' puts P inside NUT, after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is the data or advice taken in by a person or a computer.

clue.text: Story provided by Catholic and Anglican organisation

parts.note: Roman as in Roman Catholic
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A tale put out jointly by Catholic and Anglican bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a tale of love or adventure, a kind of story.

clue.text: Student of the sun's written about carbon and hydrogen

indicators.note: written about means the sun word is written around the chemical symbols

parts.note: solar means of the sun
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A student of the sun has written a paper on carbon and hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' wraps SOLAR round CH, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or one who studies, so a student.
